extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, editors, bibliographers, and indexers of short stories and periodical literature
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and selection criteria for indexing and rating short stories published in American magazines between October 1919 and September 1920, including notation conventions, inclusion/exclusion rules, and magazine-ranking rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope period
rubrics_metrics.description: OCTOBER, 1919, TO SEPTEMBER, 1920 (All short stories published in the following magazines and newspapers, October, 1919 to September, 1920 inclusive, are indexed.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index covers stories published within this inclusive twelve-month period; missing issues (due to labor/transportation difficulties) will be reported next year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction system
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk stories are of somewhat permanent literary value; three-asterisk titles entitle the story to a place on the annual 'Rolls of Honor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-asterisk meaning (permanent value)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Three-asterisk stories" are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories given three asterisks are considered to have lasting literary worth and are placed on the annual Rolls of Honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise noted (e.g., (R.) indicates a reprint), reprinted stories are omitted from the counts and lists used in the analysis and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The lists often state they exclude reprints, but not translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translated stories are generally included in the counts and rankings even when reprints are excluded; some tables explicitly state 'excluding reprints, but not translations.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'distinctive'/'stories of distinction'
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain stories are labeled 'distinctive' or 'stories of distinction' (one, two, or three asterisks) and only these are counted in some tables and selectively indexed lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asterisks indicate degrees of distinction; only stories judged distinctive are included in special tallies and some selective indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine inclusion criteria for percentage table
rubrics_metrics.description: The table includes the averages of American periodicals published from October, 1919, to September, 1920 inclusive; the following tables indicate the rank, ... of the twenty-one periodicals coming within the scope of my examination which have published an average of 15 per cent in stories of distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To appear in the ranked-percentage table a periodical had to publish an average of at least 15% distinctive stories during the stated period; the examination scope is limited to listed periodicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals are ranked (a) By Percentage of Distinctive Stories and (b) By Number of Distinctive Stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate tables show rank by percent and by count; these rankings are used to evaluate periodical performance over the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the above lists have been decided by taking relative rank in other lists into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two or more periodicals tie in one list, their positions are resolved by comparing their relative placements in other relevant lists (e.g., number vs. percentage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective indexing vs. full indexing of periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: All short stories published in a set of named magazines/newspapers are indexed; 'Short stories of distinction only' from another set of magazines are indexed; certain other stories of distinction 'have been specially called to my attention' and are indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are three categories: (1) Fully indexed periodicals (all short stories in scope are indexed), (2) Periodicals indexed only for 'stories of distinction' (asterisked), and (3) Specially-noted stories from other sources included by editor's attention. The editor lists which magazines fall into each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation: asterisk before author's name
rubrics_metrics.description: An asterisk before the name of an author indicates that he is not an American.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to mark non-American authors in the index entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation: (H) after author's name
rubrics_metrics.description: (H) after the name of an author indicates that other stories by this author, published in American magazines between 1900 and 1914, are to be found indexed in 'The Standard Index of Short Stories' by Francis J. Hannigan (1918).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that the author already appears in an earlier standard index; helps cross-reference previous volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation: parenthetical figures after titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The figures in parentheses after the title of a story refer to the volume and page number of the magazine. In cases where successive numbers of a magazine are not paged consecutively, the page number only is given in this index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parenthetical citations follow the (volume: page) convention when applicable; otherwise only page numbers are given for non-consecutive pagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of standardized abbreviations is used for periodical titles (e.g., 'Dial' = Dial, 'Harper's M' = Harper's Monthly, 'N. Y. Trib' = New York Tribune).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries use these abbreviations; the index provides a key mapping each abbreviation to the full periodical name and notes special cases (e.g., exceptions of particular months/issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special inclusion note
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain stories of distinction published in the following magazines and newspapers during this period are indexed, because they have been specially called to my attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Besides the standard inclusion lists, the editor may add items brought to attention even if the source is outside the primary indexing set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Owing to labor and transportation difficulties, the files of certain periodicals which I have consulted this year are not absolutely complete. I shall report upon these missing issues next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges potential incompleteness of the index and signals forthcoming corrections or additions.
